subject.title: [Feature]: Configurable umask / file permissions for agent-created user-facing files

question: Should OpenClaw add a core `tools.fs` user-output permission policy for agent-created files, and if so what exact boundary and mode semantics should it own?
rationale: The requested fix adds config surface and deliberately changes local filesystem security behavior across multiple tool write paths, including arbitrary exec output, so code inspection cannot safely choose the product/security boundary by itself.

options.title: Add Opt-In User-Output Policy
options.body: Add a narrowly scoped config policy for user-facing outputs only, with private state excluded and tests/docs proving each write path that opts in.

options.title: Keep Narrow Fixes Separate
options.body: Leave this general policy open or deferred and address specific failures such as outbound media or private-state regressions in their narrower issues.

options.title: Decline Core Config Surface
options.body: Keep ownership with OS/container ACLs, service umask, and operator workflows, documenting that OpenClaw will not normalize user-output file modes.

recommendation.title: Add Opt-In User-Output Policy
recommendation.body: Add a narrowly scoped config policy for user-facing outputs only, with private state excluded and tests/docs proving each write path that opts in.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision spans sandbox write hardening, apply_patch, and filesystem safety boundaries where steipete has the strongest recent history signal.
